key_insight: The paper demonstrates efficient generation, distribution, and storage of three-qubit entanglement across three remote single-atom nodes in separate laboratories.
engineering_relevance: This result advances the practicality of modular quantum networks by improving the light-matter interface bottleneck that limits scaling beyond two-node entanglement.
method: Sequentially entangled atoms pairwise across three nodes
Used heralded state transfer to move and store entanglement
evidence_signal: The reported three-qubit entangled state achieved 77(1)% fidelity, an entanglement lifetime above 200 microseconds, Mermin inequality violation with the detection loophole closed, and 0.16% generation efficiency.
watch_item: The generation efficiency is still low in absolute terms, so scaling to larger multi-node networks will likely require further gains in interface performance and repetition rate.
paper_title: Efficient entanglement of three remote single-atom quantum-network nodes
